title: A covering collection of acyclic objects detects derived inverse limits
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $(\mathcal F_n,t_n)_{n\ge1}$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$. Let $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ be a set such that every object of $\mathcal C$ has a covering with all members in $\mathcal B$. Suppose that, for every $U\in\mathcal B$, $n\ge1$ and $p>0$, $H^p(U,\mathcal F_n)=0$ and $R^1\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U)=0$. Here $H^p(U,-)$ is right derived evaluation in sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules, with values in abelian groups, and $R^1\varprojlim$ on section groups is the right derived functor on abelian-group towers of [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups]. Put $\mathcal F=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n$, computed sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. In $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the natural comparison $\mathcal F[0]\to R\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n[0]$ is an isomorphism, and $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and $p>0$. The right side is computed by the right derived inverse-limit functor on the strict tower and is a derived limit in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]; the comparison is the one induced by the ordinary limit into that derived functor.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $K=R\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to this strict degree-zero tower: $K$ exists and has the derived-limit triangle with projections $p_n:K\to\mathcal F_n[0]$. Let $c:\mathcal F[0]\to K$ be the specified right-derived comparison. Its composites with $p_n$ are the ordinary limit projections $\pi_n[0]$. Indeed, on a K-injective tower resolution $q:\mathcal F_\bullet[0]\to I_\bullet$, $K$ is represented by $\lim I_n$ and $c$ by $\lim q_n$; its $n$th projection is $q_n\pi_n$. Localizing and identifying $QI_n$ with $\mathcal F_n[0]$ gives the asserted equality. Here the ordinary sectionwise limit and its coordinate projections are those of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit].

source.place: Tag 0BKY (lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit), proof; with Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim) and Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology).

proof.text: For any module sheaf $M$, choose its injective resolution in degrees $\geq0$. Such resolutions are available: [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] makes $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck, and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies injective embeddings; successively embed the cokernel of $M\hookrightarrow J^0$, then the next cokernel, to construct $J^\bullet$. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Thus $H^m(U,M[0])$ is computed by $J^\bullet(U)$, vanishes for $m<0$, and for $m=0$ is $M(U)$: $M=\ker(J^0\to J^1)$ and kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This identification is the canonical augmentation and is natural in $M$. For $M=\mathcal F_n$ and $U\in\mathcal B$, the assumed positive-degree vanishing therefore gives $H^m(U,\mathcal F_n[0])=0$ for $m\ne0$ and $H^0(U,\mathcal F_n[0])=\mathcal F_n(U)$.

source.place: Tag 0BKY (lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit), proof; with Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim) and Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology).

proof.text: For each $U\in\mathcal B$, [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] identifies $R\Gamma(U,K)$, with its actual projections, as a derived limit of $R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F_n[0])$. Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ to obtain, for every integer $m$, $0\to R^1\lim_n H^{m-1}(U,\mathcal F_n[0])\to H^m(U,K)\xrightarrow{e_U^m}\lim_n H^m(U,\mathcal F_n[0])\to0$. Reindex $n\geq1$ by $n-1\geq0$ if necessary. Step 2 makes both outer terms zero for $m\notin\{0,1\}$, gives $H^1(U,K)=R^1\lim_n\mathcal F_n(U)=0$ by hypothesis, and makes $e_U^0:H^0(U,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim_n\mathcal F_n(U)$ an isomorphism. Its coordinates are induced by $p_n$. Consequently $e_U^0\circ H^0(U,c)$ is the coordinate identification $\mathcal F(U)=\lim_n\mathcal F_n(U)$, by Step 1 and the natural degree-zero identification in Step 2. Thus $H^0(U,c)$ is an isomorphism, and $H^m(U,K)=0$ for every $m\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0BKY (lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit), proof; with Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim) and Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology).

proof.text: For any $E\in D(\mathcal A)$ choose a K-injective representative $J$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and put $P_E^m(U)=H^m(J(U))=H^m(U,E)$. This is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules. Its sheafification is $\mathcal H^m(E)$, naturally in $E$: in presheaves write $P_E^m=\ker(d_J^m)/\operatorname{im}(d_J^{m-1})$; exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] carries this kernel/image quotient to the same quotient in sheaves, namely $\mathcal H^m(E)$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Each term of $J$ is already a sheaf, so its sheafification is itself. The identifications commute with maps because the kernel and quotient factorizations are functorial. This proves the needed ringed-site sheafification calculation directly from exactness.

source.place: Tag 0BKY (lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit), proof; with Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim) and Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology).

proof.text: For $m\ne0$ the map $0\to P_K^m$ is locally bijective: every object has a covering by $U\in\mathcal B$, and on those members $P_K^m(U)=0$ by Step 3. For $m=0$ the natural map $\mathcal F\to P_K^0$ induced by $c$ and Step 2 is bijective on every $U\in\mathcal B$ by Step 3. It is locally injective and locally surjective on every object by restricting an equality, or a target section, to such a covering. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] to both maps. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the module sheafification of a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules has as underlying abelian sheaf its abelian sheafification, with the same unit map, so these abelian isomorphisms are the underlying maps of the module sheafifications. Step 4 identifies their sheafifications with $0\to\mathcal H^m(K)$ for $m\ne0$ and with $\mathcal H^0(c):\mathcal F\to\mathcal H^0(K)$ for $m=0$. Thus the former cohomology sheaves vanish and the latter morphism is an isomorphism. These are module-sheaf isomorphisms: the inverse of a bijective linear morphism is linear, since applying the morphism to $a f^{-1}(y)$ gives $ay$.

source.place: Tag 0BKY (lemma-inverse-limit-is-derived-limit), proof; with Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim) and Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology).

proof.text: The complex $\mathcal F[0]$ has cohomology $\mathcal F$ in degree zero and zero otherwise, directly from its differential. Step 5 therefore proves that every $\mathcal H^m(c)$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], $c$ itself is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A)$. For $U\in\mathcal B$ applying the functor $H^p(U,-)$ to $c$ now identifies $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ with $H^p(U,K)$, which is zero for $p>0$ by Step 3. This is the asserted higher-cohomology vanishing as well as the comparison for the specified strict-tower derived limit.
